name: Nihon Minimal (日本のミニマル)
description: Nihon Minimal (日本のミニマル) — the refined austerity of modern Japanese design, from Muji to Naoto Fukasawa, where less is enough

foundation.story: Modern Japanese minimalism synthesizes Zen Buddhist emptiness (空, kū) with industrial design precision. Kenya Hara's 'designing white,' Naoto Fukasawa's 'without thought' (無意識のデザイン), and the Muji philosophy of 'no-brand quality goods' all express the same insight: beauty emerges when you remove everything unnecessary. The palette is almost achromatic — warmth from natural materials, not color.
foundation.philosophy: 無印 (Mujirushi) — no-brand, the beauty of nothing; emptiness as fullness

seedColors.name: Sumi-iro (墨色)
seedColors.tradition: Concentrated sumi ink — the near-black achieved when an ink stick is ground long on a suzuri stone. The default text tone in Muji packaging and Naoto Fukasawa's product design.

seedColors.name: Kinari (生成)
seedColors.tradition: The natural color of undyed, unbleached cotton or silk. Central to the Muji aesthetic — purity without the sterility of white.

seedColors.name: Hai-iro (灰色)
seedColors.tradition: Ash grey — the color of burned incense, weathered wood, and concrete. Japan's most versatile neutral, present in Tadao Ando's architecture.

seedColors.name: Asagi (浅葱)
seedColors.tradition: Pale onion-skin blue-green — a restrained hint of color from nature. Used sparingly in tea ceremony utensils and Edo-period textiles as the subtlest accent.
seedColors.source: The Colors of Japan, Sadao Hibi
